headline: Critical PHP flaws prompt emergency patches, mass website shutdowns, exploitation
summary: PHP's security team warned of two critical flaws, dubbed PHP2Shell, and rushed out emergency patches. Governments and companies across Europe and Canada took sites offline as a precaution; Amazon said attackers had already been exploiting the bugs for days before the patches shipped. OpenAI said its AI model helped find the flaws, affecting roughly 70% of websites, and researchers later found an exploit bypassing the fix, plus a further unpatched RCE flaw.

claims.statement: The PHP security team warned admins of two critical flaws and said emergency patches were coming, after details reportedly leaked ahead of schedule.

sources.quote: PHP warns admins of two critical flaws, emergency patches coming tomorrow
PHP warns it plans to release 2 emergency patches imminently

claims.statement: The two flaws, tracked together as "PHP2Shell" with CVE identifiers CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, received emergency patches from PHP.

sources.quote: The PHP security team released emergency security patches for two critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) tracked collectively as PHP2Shell.

claims.statement: PHP developers rated the vulnerabilities as critical and warned they could take websites down.

sources.quote: A critical PHP vulnerability may take websites down today

claims.statement: Government websites in several EU countries and Canada, including Belgian, Dutch, Finnish, French and German sites, were taken offline as a precaution.

sources.quote: Government websites in the EU and Canada taken offline over PHP vulnerability
Belgian, Dutch, Finnish, French and German sites were among those that governments took down temporarily as

claims.statement: Well-known sites including 4chan, DeviantArt and Wikipedia were among those hit by the issue.

sources.quote: Two bugs found with AI are behind major issues today for 4chan, DeviantArt, Wikipedia, and the blog where the bar around the corner posts pictures of people's dogs.

claims.statement: Amazon said attackers had been exploiting the vulnerabilities for about four days before the public patches were released.

sources.quote: Amazon Web Services logged attempts to leverage the internet-melting PHP2Shell bugs four days ago. They're now being “broadly exploited” across the internet.
Amazon says PHP2Shell exploitation began 4 days before patches
Hackers got a four-day head start on epic PHP2Shell vulnerability

claims.statement: Cloudflare reported millions of exploit attempts against the vulnerability.

sources.quote: Cloudflare reports millions of exploit attempts
Websites around the world have been hit by millions of attempts to exploit

claims.statement: The flaw affects PHP, a programming language used by roughly 70% of websites.

sources.quote: OpenAI says ChatGPT Sol helped uncover critical PHP flaws that could affect 70% of websites

claims.statement: OpenAI said researchers using its GPT-5.6 "Sol" model helped uncover the two critical flaws, which had severity scores of 9.2.

sources.quote: OpenAI says researchers using GPT-5.6 Sol uncovered two critical PHP vulnerabilities with severity scores of 9.2 and demonstrated working exploits, after which the company coordinated fixes.

claims.statement: Even after patches, an exploit for the vulnerability was found that bypassed the protections meant to stop remote code execution.

sources.quote: PHP2Shell exploit bypasses protections designed to stop remote code execution

claims.statement: IT and cybersecurity workers described the response to the flaw as relentless in the days after disclosure.

sources.quote: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

claims.statement: Cybersecurity leaders said AI helped uncover the long-hidden flaws and warned the episode signals AI will expose more infrastructure weaknesses.

sources.quote: AI uncovered long-hidden programming flaws, triggering a rare global cyber-security response.
After discovery of severe bug in the PHP programming language, executives warn of ‘vulnerability tsunami’

claims.statement: Days later, PHP shared mitigation steps for a further, newly found remote code execution vulnerability affecting non-default configurations, for which no patch yet existed.

sources.quote: The PHP security team has shared mitigation measures for a new remote code execution vulnerability that affects systems with non-default configurations and has no patch.
PHP2Shell: Haven’t patched yet? Take these steps now to mitigate

claims.statement: The UK worked to identify its exposure after the global warning, as Amazon said it had seen attacks before the warning went public.

sources.quote: Governments and companies are scrambling to protect their websites, as Amazon says it experienced attacks before the warning was made public.
